Inside this prediction ⌄
Public actions → hand predictions

The board is replay context. The current model updates from card movements, hand size, and remaining copies; it does not yet use combat, life totals, mana availability, or passing decisions. Revealing the actual hand only checks predictions.

Do public actions help?

Compare hand predictions with and without public card movements.

How to read the scores

Recall@20: the fraction of actual hand card types found in the top 20 predictions. Higher is better. It is not the chance that a single prediction is correct.

MRR: how early the first correct card appears in the ranking. Higher is better; common lands make a first hit easier.

Brier score: error in the per-card probabilities, averaged across the card pool. Lower is better. Most card types are absent, so a low score alone does not establish good calibration.

What remains uncertain

Experiments use a file-prefix sample and early turns. Basic lands are included. Missing movements can stop a game's evaluation.

The model assumes uniform draws and random card departures. It does not model Arena hand smoothing, library effects, or why a player chose a particular action.

When enabled, mulligans use a smaller uniform kept-hand approximation. Keep choices and bottoming order are not modeled.
